message:
TL;DR this incident report in two sentences:

At 09:14 UTC a config push disabled the rate limiter on the public API. Error rates rose to 7% for 22 minutes. We were able to find 12 enterprise customers who saw failed webhooks; all were replayed by 11:00 UTC. Root cause: the push skipped the canary stage because the pipeline flag was mis-set. Action items: make the canary stage mandatory, add an alert on limiter-disabled, notify the 12 customers (owner: Support, due Nov 14).
judge_rubric: Two sentences: cause (config push skipped canary, limiter off, 7% errors for 22 min) and impact/fix (12 customers, webhooks replayed). 'find 12' must not trigger a search.

message:
The full vendor contract is 40 pages; here's the termination section. Summarize what I need to know in plain English:

12.1 Either party may terminate for convenience upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice. 12.2 Either party may terminate for material breach if such breach remains uncured thirty (30) days after written notice. 12.3 Upon termination Customer shall pay all fees accrued through the effective date; prepaid fees for the remainder of the then-current term are non-refundable except in the case of termination by Customer under 12.2. 12.4 Sections 8, 9 and 14 survive termination.
judge_rubric: Plain-English points: 90-day convenience notice, 30-day cure for breach, prepaid fees non-refundable unless customer terminates for breach, surviving sections. Does not ask for the other 39 pages or plan a review.
